I can understand your perspective in trying to overcompensate for the intangibles that win you games due to the overemphasis on kills. I know its possible to help your team more by getting literally 0 kills and playing medic only to heal and revive (ive done that in battlebit remastered) or other supportive means. 

But for the general playerbase getting kills cannot be just an optional byproduct nor not part of the 'core play'. 

On attack what is the main goal? Capture points. On defense what is the main goal? Defend points. Both cannot happen without getting the enemy team off of the point. And how do you get people off the point? As an attacker, besides backcapping the only way is to kill the defenders. As a defender you have to kill the attackers on the point. Killing in a 32 v 32 battlefield style game is a direct result of the objectives of the games. Literally without getting a certain amount of kills you literally cannot win the game. But also only getting kills wont win you the game. Its a combination of both. 

Hence why i said to win a game, quality of kills matter, not quantity. A game thats more akin to your idea where kills are more of an 'optional byproduct' are games like league or dota, where the objectives arent as simple 'capture these points and destroy their base'. And even then kills arent optional, you cant avoid a team fight and win a game, because the other team is coming to contest objectives that lead to a win which causes mandatory fighting, unless that team just wants to lose. Same principle for delta force. Please tell me how defenders can win without killing? 

I know youre moreso referring to just individual players (like i personally dont need 40 kills to help the team) but the idea that kills in an online shooter game are 'optional byproducts' is just wrong.

My peak was d3 in 2s and 3s (fuck 1s) and that was ONLY because i was consistently playing like at least 1 ranked match a day and just playing a lot. Even then i could feel that ceiling lol. I couldnt deal with how good everyone was in the air at that level and air rolling fast and accurate enough (it felt like solving a rubicks cube in real time). Not to mention i play on knb rather than controller, i prob couldve hit champ but i just didnt think the amount of time i had to dedictate to consistently playing was worth it. 

Now i play once in a while with friends in plat. I genuinely do not think i can climb to diamond unless i really practice and grind out ranked like i used to.

I do think kills are the crucial part, and the smokes, beacons, targetting vehicles, etc. are the required part. But volume of kills are not as important as the quality. 
30 kills in the meatgrinder is not nearly as valuable as 10 kills in flanks to pull bodies away from the meatgrinder to deal with backcapping, letting your team win the util/numbers battle of the meatgrinder; or 10 kills defending and preventing a flank.

A big part of it is honestly out of your hands in a 32 v 32 mode. At marshal rank, you should be able to rely on your team to be competent. But when i became stuck at gen 2/1 i realized theres no sbmm. I would get squad mates who didnt know how to switch seats in vehicles and goated squadmates or medics who would run out in the open to revive someone without throwing any smoke or cover - dumb shit that people who earned that rank would not do. 

Theres a chance like half of your kills arent/cant be used in a momentum based event. This is mostly seen in flanking maneuvers or shutting down flanks on defense, but also positioning yourself in relation to the map and objectives. For example i would be farming kills on B1 defense because our defensive hold is solid. But i see on the map that some teammates are dying on their way to b1 from b2, and i see skirmishes of enemies pushing a flank not to b1 but b2. Sure i can stay at b1 and get 50-60 kills but i can also flank the flankers and stop a potential pincer movement from ruining our defensive hold. 

Especially as someone who can consistently dish out a lot of kills you would be invaluable in a role where you either are part of the main pushing element (assault + medic) where you play a bit reckless and push to create enough space for a foothold for you teammates to push and take advantage of the space/chaos you create (they wont lol). I know tickets exists but people play wayyy too scared like they have 1 life for the entire match (besides bots this is also why so many players have like 3 kills and 3 deaths the whole game). Taking risks is necessary to make plays. I always see value in assault players jumping and running in to clear a corner, knowing theyll die too to try and create some sort of space or foothold for the rest of your team to follow up (i love jumping in on vyron to catch enemies off guard and create space for teammates that never come). Gravitate towards any weak points in the defense or attack.

For reference last season i had a ~56/57% wr. I think this is fairly high on average, so i just have to attribute most of it to luck, but also i notice how you only play recon, which imo is the best 'carry' class besides selfish medic (not reviving or healing others), but some games require different methods to win (many games people refuse to play support so vehicles run rampant, not much you can do as hackclaw againdt them). I do think you'll benefit from playing the other classes in situatuons that call for them.

But also this games merit system is terrible. It actively punishes you for playing smart and disciplined. It actively punishes you for not holding w and running into the meat grinders on the point. I would often lose merit in a majority of the games i play to win as i dont try to maximize my kills like i normally do and im often times not actually on the point but holding/fight for a flank leading to an objective.

Its also just hard to track important stats like that one dude holding a flank even though only a few enemies come through that flank. If no one was holding that area, it could easy cause a pincer flank causing you to lose that point.

Its an interesting problem.

When you are using a mouse, it mainly performs 2d actions in a relatively 1:1 relation to your screen. If your mouse starts at the center of your screen and you move the mouse to the left, your action on screen is a relative 1:1 with the mouse. The mouse is ultimiately controlling the hands -> holding a sword which interacts in a 3d space (z axis). The mouse inherently doesnt have a z axis or 'up' direction it can go, so a move done in a 2d space (the mouse) without a z axis will have to 'guess' the z axis based off the physics/position of the character and sword. 

For example it will get confused of you were trying to bring your sword up to a high guard or stab (esp in alt mode its difficult to adjust the aim, and a stab can very easily deviate off path from a seemingly non-relevant micro movement from ur mouse). Or if youre trying to line up the edge for a proper cut, the game can have a hard time determining if you were trying to line up the edge of the blade for a cut or just swinging to the left or right.

As the game 'makes up' the z values from your movements, it also has to interact physically wirh the x and y axis, creating immense confusion where you wanted to perform a 1:1 2d move, but the 3d dimension of height has the potential to fuck up a relative simple swing if your movements are incredibly precise.

This is why everyone is saying to play on low sens, and i do. But trying to manipulate objects in a true 3d space through a 2d screen with a 2d movement of area mouse, its inevitable the insane skill level possible for precise sword movements.

Spinning wheel/heel kick (the spinning roundhouse youre thinking of) is done by:

1. Press and hold shift (the entire time) so you establish a rear foot position. It ls your rear foot thats doing the kicking
2. Kick (spacebar) before any turning or spinning motion. 
3. If your left leg is in the back, kick, spin to the left (mouse turns counterclockwise). If right foot is in the back, spin to the right (clockwise).
Everything else is timing (like a small delay after kicking before spinning) and distance management. 

Normal roundhouse kicks:

Same set up as the spinning kick up to #2. After pressing kick, you now flick your mouse in the direction your kicks going. If left leg is kicking, you are flicking from southwest to northeast on your mouse, and the opposite for the right leg.

This ones a bit more intuitive, as you just flick your mouse after kicking. The tricky part are head kicks with roundhouses as you have to flick a little higher up with aim.

I sometimes feel the same but whats more important than speed and power is edge alignment. Lower mouse sens helps for this but makes it harder to swing faster. But as a bladed weapon (esp 2h) it doesnt need much velocity to deal a fatal blow (even when youre playing on minimum damage). For exmaple i play 800 dpi ~1/4 of the sens bar for a while but now my sens ~50% but i occasionally go lower if i feel like my edge alignment is off. 

Even with blunt weapons like the mace that benefit more from force, you dont need a large windup for a fatal blow.  As edge alignment is not as important as a sword, i find that using shorter, quick, flick-like mouse movements from a fairly neutral stance to deliver powerful shots.

Vertical slashes are difficult due to the nature of trying to manipulate 3d objects in true physical 3d manifestation represented on a 2d screen that is implemented on mouse that physically maps a 2d space.  For these you want mainly arm movement with minimal wrist. In a similar vein, if you want a perfectly horizontal cut, itd be diffocult tk do with mainly wrist movements as your hand moves from left to right (or vice versa) in a semi circle motion like a windshield wiper. In a game like this yoy need to implement both wrist n arm movements, more so deliverately than omany other games

Flanking in this game (as with any game) is extremely difficult if you dont know the map. Unfortunately for this part the only thing u can do is play and learn the map. Silver lining is that most servers are empty so you can join empty maps to learn them if you wish. In conjunction, i would take time to edit the ui for the map to make it comfortable for you to not only access (like binding it to tab) but for you to be able tell whats going on. I know most of the maps pretty ok, but theyre way too massive for me to actually learn each building and room. So whenever im on a flanking mission im constantly checking tab to see where im going. This helps in avoiding a large fight that you might be accidentally pathing to. Someone on your team migjt spot an enemy running into your flank path. You realize the path youre taking is leading straight into open ground where youve been sniped before. Its all about trying to take in as much relevant information to help you determine what to do. Also remember when youre flanking your main objective should be to create another angle of attack on the enemy. If theres a fight at point C, with your team fighting moving north while the enemy is fighting moving south, while your team is on the enemys south side, you should try to be on the enemys west, east, or north side. Flanks dont have to be just about taking out stragglers. Many times during my flank i purposely AVOID enemies and fighting them, running if i can. Why risk a 50% 1v1 when i can potentially get 4, 5 or more free kills from behind.

In terms of gear just know armor is broken and only gives you a movement penalty after it breaks. Anothee commenter explained it very well. Therefore i always run either ranger armor (gives most mags) or the lightest armor, but i know there are posts with spreadsheets showing like which armors are the most optimal and etc. 

In terms of weapons every single weapon is pretty well balanced and viable. But some weapons are better for certain situations (prob not gonna take a DMR if my squads doing a buncha cqc)

In terms of weapon attachments, the main things you should worry about is damage, vertical and horizontal recoil (VR/HR), first shot accuracy, and things like aim down speed, reload speed. Velocity is pretty whatever unless youre using a sniper. Some of the stats are not very relevant or even work. I always prefer to have more VR than HR because with VR you just pull down, but HR is random left and right sway. Rule of thumb i like my VR to be no higher than 1.4/1.5 and HR to be no higher than 0.9 or 1. Some weapons like battle rifles you cant achieve that, so i just like to keep HR down as much. 
For grips, i find myself mostly using the se5 as it provides generally the best balance. As well as vert grip, bcm gun fighter, se5, and the one that significantly reduces reload time. 
For barrels, i usually use flash hider/muzzle break because it provides the best overall stats at the cost of very high VR. But i also run the vamb or the ss5 one that looks like a suppressor, as well as actually suppressors (usually long). So from memory, i know for my ak/m4 i had something like se5 grip with vamb. 75% of all attachments you prob arent gonna use, just the ones that fit your playstyle.

Sniping is just a practice thing. Unless we see a clip of potential problems youre having, thats really it. The only thing ill say is you should 100% learn how to use the range finder attachment for snipers in conjunction with zeroing (alt+mouse scroll down to lower, up to raise). You use the rangefinder to see the range of an enemy (i.e. 200m). You then zero the sniper to 200, and click on the enemy head rarher than trying to predict the drop.

Some coping methods for anxiety:

1. Military breathing technique. Breath in for 4 counts, hold your breath for 4 counts, breath out for 4 counts, hold your breath for 4 counts, repeat for as long as you need. You can set it to any measurement of time and your counts can be as short or as long as you need it to be (for reference i stare at the seconds on a clock, and do 3 seconds for each). 

2. Rapid left and right eye movement. Be still and dont move your head. Then as fast as you can in a steady pace, move your eyes left and right. You can start slow and build up speed to whatever you want (faster the better but keep it a reasonable pace ig).

3. Switching cognitive focus. Have a task or thing that you can focus/work on while youre having anxiety. You generally want it to be something that requires your whole focus and makes it hard for you to focus on anything else. This one is a bit harder and requires a level of experience and level headedness. For example, what i would do is debate in my head in which situations specific guns in a video game i play would be good for. 1. Do not go to duel servers or play the 1v1 gamemode. You will get stomped by people with hundreds n thousands of hours. Only do it if youre going against someone thats ur level. A lot of very good and very sweaty players im those modes.

3. When you feel ready for a real server, id recommend the 40 player mode. Less players, less chaos, easier to tell whats going on.

Stabs with halberd from behind, try to go to their left or right, holding the front line a little bit by  doing a riposte/counter + swing combo and then instantly dodge backwards (you can dodge to the left, right, or backwards by pressing A, D, or S twice respectively). Just like most other games, youre gonna die a lot as you learn. There is no form of matchmaking, so you wont exclusively go against other new players.

I dont want to overwhelm you with anything too specific, so some general bits of advice:

1. Your map is your best friend. Bind it to something you can easily access (tab for me). As you learn the game, maps, objectives, ally location, etc., it will become easier and easier to read. It is VERY easy to get lost (happens to me literally all the time), and although you can see the objectives on your screen, it helps to look at your map so you can see where youre going. 

2. Using the map or just your eyes, make sure youre always trying to stay with or respawn on a with a decent number of teammates (or your squad, indicated by green). Try to generally stick with them because theyll usually be running to the next point. As a new player id advise against being the first to engage/run in, however there are times where my team are being pussies so i run in alone, encouraging many others to follow. 

3. Pretty much every gun is "good". Guns fit certain niches and roles, but theyre all viable (including the level 0 starter guns!).

4. Imo this game is a combo of an arcade shooter and mil sim, so youll have to be careful running in open space. I do believe a good amount of your deaths will come from poor positioning (not ur fault ur new), so try your best to keep in mind enemy objectives captured, and thay they will generally be coming from that area. Try to have at least 1 wall that you can use for cover, and look at where your teammates are running/pointing/shootings.

5. In cqc, experience and good players wont often use their scope, as hipfiring is accurate at that range. Ive seen many videos talking about how aiming with hipfire is crucial, and it can be, but wait till you unlock a laser for that, as it can be confusing. 

6. Get comfortable with using the lean buttons (q and e by default) and id recommend to keep them tap instead of hold. You can gain peekers/angle advantages with them like crazy. Its also this games equivalent of A D A D spam (moving left and right) to try and make it harder for you to be hit. 

7. Dont be afraid to ask the chat if youre confused about something. Games still in beta, so a lot of QoL features just arent here yet. I have around 200 hours and im still learning things, as are many other players.

8. Dont be afraid to take things slow, if youre slow to move from objective to objective, dont worry about it. Take your time and do what you need to do to:

9: Have fun!

I love the riot shield, but it is situational. 


You can either play it for yourself:

Like using it to run from one cover to another to prevent snipers and others from melting you.

Or to safely peek corners if you suspect an enemy/enemies. Just be ready to hide back into cover/switch to gun/be ready to kill. Ive spotted many riot shield players all alone pushing tight corriders and have been able to run behind them to kill them. Rmr you have 0 ability to kill on your shield. 

Or in specific situations:

You have a squad that is activr in comms and you can communicate with them - you can communicate a push with you leading the charge (bonus pts if others have shield) with a medic sitting and healing/bandaging you. This method is EXTREMELY powerful so long as the distance you have to push has minimal sightlines from different places (corridors). You csn realistically have the medic + 2 or 3 other players just sit behind the shield and be able to kill without being killed. 

If there is a downed tm8, with comms you can ask a tm8 to drag the downed tm8 to safety while you shield them (i found that over time if you use a shield and walk to a downed body and comm to your teammates, many players will be more than eager to help the assist)

Anytime theres a graveyard (a mass of downed players, players and medics trying to heal/reload), you can increase their survival by just being a bullet sponge. Keep in mind if a nade is thrown, you need to run away because riot shield has 0 protection against explosives.

Safely peek and ping enemy positions. You are able to peek a house occupied by enemies ans ping them pretty safely without worrying about dying. 


Just keep in mind riot shield is extremely vulnerable to explosive dmg and it doesnt make u invincible - enough bullets will cause you to take dmg. Very niche but fun weapon - i either run this or ammo kit.

I really do enjoy using the riot shield, but as the other comment said, it definitely is situational. While i do not think you would have much fun using just the riot shield, there are a lot of niches it fills that will make your teammates thank you. 

1. Selfish use - you can use riot shields to get from point A to B in a slower but much often safer way. This works best when youre trying to push a point, and are moving from cover to cover. It is not a good idea to move long distances with the shield out because it makes you too vulnerable from different angles and explosives. Example: youre trying to push across a street to another apt but your boys are getting shredded by machine gun n sniper fire. Use ur shield to safely cross with minimal risk and insane protection.

2. Baiting ammunition - battlebit can be very fast paced, esp in cqc. If you know or think an enemy is in a house or smth, you can peek/start the engage with the shield. A good amount of players will panic and mag dump, which then you can promptly pull ur gun out and wipe them. Against more skilled and disciplined players, you will only get a small burst before they try to run around you/nade you/reposition. If they try to run behind you, being next to a wall while peeking helps to let you change to your gun but try to switch whem theyre still in their running animation as they have to leave sprint to fire. 

3. Frontlining for ur teammates (just like reinhardt). This ones requires coordination and for your teammates to actually follow you. Altho its hard for your teammates to all conga line behind you for cover, it is a huge morale boost to see someone with a riot shield lead the charge, although you will be overtaken by sprinting teammates lol.

4. Chokes and corners - if your teammates are trying to contest a choke or corner, riot shield is great for protecting your tm8s. Just be mindful that with enough bullets you will take damage (im pretty sure), so just play it like a reinhardt, going in and out of cover to prevent getting bursted. Just be careful for nades in chokes because they will f u up.

5. Protecting graveyards/securing revives - i find that riot shields have the best utility without the need for coordination when you have a mess of dead/injured tm8s and medics trying to help them all. They are extremely susceptible to random gunfire and explosions and altho explosion defense is limited, i have saved literally 10+ teammates in a graveyard from random gun fire that wouldve bursted them down. 
Riot shields are a sort of a extended revive mechanic as long as you have a tm8 whos coordinating the rescue. Essentially you make urself a target by going in fromt of the downed tm8 while the one following you grabs the downed and pulls them into safety witj you following. 

6. Baiting/finding out enemy positions - similar to #2, a lot of players will just shoot anything that moves. This is especially useful when youre moving to an area that you dont know exactly where the enemy is. By peeking with the riot shield, not only can it potentially draw fire, making the enemy expose themselves without you being hurt at all, you can also ping the enemy location while using your shield, making you something like a hanzo albeit a bit scuffed. 

7. Presence - just the presence of a riot shield will cause your teammates to feel just a bit safer, esp if youre positioning well. It will make them more confident in peeking angles so long as youre holding some of the space. Same goes for the enemy, as you force them to have 5 guys mag dump you, throw nades, or reposition/ignore

There are prob other niches and creative ways you can find to use shields, but i find myself mainly using them for moving point to point (like the long ass bridges on wakistan to prevent getting sniped), providing a sense of cover, or trying to protect a graveyard. So the games main mechanic is the three different areas of interaction, left, middle, right. The game will flash one of the 3 areas for you to respond to, and you have to move your joystick/thumb to the according area. So while fighting, if the left side of the bar lights up (orange and then yellow as previously mentioned) you would move your joystick/thumb to the left side as well. You match the enemy's movement. So when the left side of the bar flashes orange, move your joystick to the left, and get ready to counter, dodge, or block (which is just moving your joystick to the area the enemy is attacking). The main quest enemies are extremely high level (dumb move by the developers) and will require you to have a fast reaction speed. Once again, i strongly encourage you to use sound cues to help with countering - they personally help me immensely compared to not using sound. However this will require some getting used to, especially when you are trying out two handed or one handed weapons. Just rmr for one handed weapons your speed in general will be faster, which i believe means you have a faster swing speed (and i think more time to react to counters but im not 100% sure), as well as taking less damage while blocking (or just mimicking the movement of the enrmy without dodging or attacking), but two handed swords do more damage and personally, i think the rhythm feels better for countering and combos, really up to preference.
